To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA synthetic response to mevalonates of both normal and abnormal human peripheral blood lymphoid cells can be significantly enhanced when these cells are incubated with granulocytes.
neutrophils provide help to lymphocytes in the DNA synthetic and mitotic response to mevalonolactone and that this help is not mediated by the production of a mevalonate- derived growth factor.
mevalonic acid is a mitogen for human peripheral blood B lymphocytes and that the DNA synthetic response is augmented by granulocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of cellular growth and differentiation by the mevalonate pathway.
the regulation of cellular metabolism and mitosis by the isoprenoid metabolites of mevalonic and acetic acid.
the regulation of DNA synthesis and mitotic activity in normal and malignant cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mevalonate stimulates lymphocyte DNA synthesis by acting on a mevalonate-responsive lymphocyte subpopulation, which, in the presence of granule-free neutrophils, can synthesize DNA at a level comparable to the DNA synthetic response observed in normal peripheral blood lymphocyte populations.

the mevalonate-induced stimulation of lymphocyte DNA synthesis is a complex phenomenon that is influenced by the presence of neutrophils, the nature of the cells, and the state of activation of both cell types.
the granulocytes, in the presence of mevalonates, are able to stimulate lymphocytes to enter the cell cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mevalonate is an effective mitogen for normal E rosettes-negative cells, but that the response of these cells can be further enhanced by the addition of neutrophils.
mevalonic acid stimulates DNA synthesis in human peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures by two mechanisms.
mevalonic acid is a potent stimulator of DNA synthesis and mitogenesis in human lymphocytes, but only when the lymphocytes are exposed to mevalonic-acid-treated cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neutrophil granulocytes are important accessory cells in the mevalonate-induced DNA synthetic response of E rosette negative lymphocytes.

mevalonic acid does not directly trigger lymphocyte DNA synthesis, but that it is an important intermediate in the synthesis of a growth factor that is produced by neutrophils and is required for the initiation of DNA synthesis.
the mevalonate pathway in normal cells is regulated in such a way as to limit the synthesis of mevalonolactone, the precursor to the mevalonatederived growth factor.
